svg.title: Market risk desk dashboard — Analytical Canvas variant
svg.desc: Static desktop mockup of a market-risk dashboard screen using illustrative synthetic data. A page-wide method selector (Historical Simulation, Parametric, Monte Carlo) drives every panel. Four headline metrics show VaR 99% one-day of 4.82 million US dollars, Expected Shortfall 97.5% one-day of 5.14 million, an approximate 10-day VaR 99% of 15.24 million derived by square-root-of-ten scaling, and 4 backtest exceptions over 250 days against 2.5 expected. A P&L distribution histogram of 500 historical scenarios marks the VaR and Expected Shortfall quantiles, shades the 1 percent tail in red and the remaining 97.5 to 99 percent band in amber, and lists the worst scenarios in a tail-detail card showing that Expected Shortfall 97.5% is the mean of the worst 2.5 percent of scenarios, that is the worst 12 observations plus half weight on the 13th, 12.5 in total. A component VaR panel lists Rates 1.94, Credit 1.28, Equity 0.86, FX 0.49 and Commodity 0.25, which sum exactly to the 4.82 total with zero residual, while the 1.93 diversification benefit is reported on a separate reconciling line rather than allocated to components. A 60-day backtest chart plots realised daily profit and loss against the VaR threshold line and highlights 2 exceptions in the window.

g.text: Illustrative synthetic data — not a production risk report
Daily revalued P&L, USD millions. Red is beyond VaR 99%; amber completes the 2.5% ES tail.
97.5–99% band — rest of the ES tail
Components sum exactly to total VaR 99% 1-day.
shown as a standalone reconciling line.
Bars: realised daily P&L. Line: VaR threshold. Marked days breach the threshold.
• All figures are illustrative synthetic values generated for design review; they do not describe any real portfolio or institution.
• ES 97.5% averages the worst 2.5% of the 500-scenario set — the worst 12 observations at full weight plus the 13th at half weight (12.5 in total).
• 10-day VaR is a √10 scaling of the 1-day figure, shown in neutral to flag that it is an approximation rather than a 10-day resimulation.
• Component VaR is additive and reconciles to total VaR with zero residual; the diversification benefit is reported as a separate line, never allocated.
• Backtest uses clean P&L against the same method selected page-wide. Exception counts and Basel zone bands are shown for context only.

svg.text: Screen 1 of 1 · Concept: Analytical Canvas · Static mockup, 1280px desktop
Synthetic data · No investment or regulatory advice
